Complainant : K.R. Puram Tr PS  Bangalore  (Rep by: State by Sr. APP)
 V/s  Accused : Shankar Naika  S/o. Kabbalu Naika  Aged about 39 years  R/at: Near Ganesha Temple  Sarjapur, Bangalore - 571 313  (Rep by : Adv Sri. KKA)
 1. Date of commission of offence : 07.01.2017  2. Offence alleged : P/U/S. 279, 304(A) IPC  3. Date of recording of evidence : 01.02.2024  4. Date of Judgment : 07.01.2026  JUDGMENT

This case arises from the charge sheet filed by the PI of KR. Puram Traffic P. S. In Cr. No. 21/2017 against the accused for the alleged offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) IPC.
C.C. No. 13438/2017 2.
The brief facts of the prosecution's case are as follows:
On 01.07.2017 at 09.35 p.m., the accused was the driver of Lorry No. AP 27 TU 3949.

He drove his Lorry on FCI Godown Road near Sudhir Way Bridge, from the old Madras Road towards FCI Godown, in a rash and negligent manner, to endanger human safety and dashed into a pedestrian, Sri Venkateshappa, who was crossing the Kr Puram Tr Ps vs Shankar Naika on 7 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15157879/

Thereby, the accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) IPC.
3.
After receipt of the complaint, the investigating officer visited the spot, conducted a mahazar in the presence of mahazar witnesses.
Inquired and obtained statements of witnesses.

After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet was filed against the accused for the offences p/u/s. 279,
304(A) IPC.
4.

After filing the Charge Sheet, this court has verified all the prosecution records and considering that there are prima facie materials to proceed further against the accused, cognizance for the alleged offence p/u/s. 279, 304(A) IPC was taken, and a criminal case was registered against the accused in a register No. III, and a process was issued against the accused.
5.
Pursuant to the summons, the accused appeared through his counsel and availed bail.

Prosecution papers were supplied to the accused as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
C.C. No. 13438/2017 6.

Heard learned Sr APP and learned counsel for the accused, as there are no grounds to discharge the accused from the case, and there are materials to adjudicate the matter, hence, the substance of the accusation was framed.
Read over and explained to the accused in the language best known to him.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
Hence, the case was posted for prosecution evidence.
Out of 13 witnesses, the prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to 6 and marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed prosecution evidence.

7. After the conclusion of the prosecution evidence, the statement of the accused as required U/s.
313 Cr.P.C
is recorded, read over and explained to the accused in the language best known to him.
The accused denied all incriminating circumstances that appeared against him in the prosecution's evidence.
However, not chosen to lead the defence evidence.
Hence, the case was posted for arguments.
8. Heard arguments canvassed by learned APP and learned counsel for the accused.
Meticulously perused documents placed on record.

9. The following points arise for my consideration; Point No.1: Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 01.07.2017 at 09.35 p.m, the accused was a driver of Lorry No.
AP 27 TU 3949 drove his lorry on the FCI godown road, near Sudhir Way Bridge, from the old Madras road towards FCI godown in C.C. No. 13438/2017 a rash and negligent manner to endanger human safety and dashed into pedestrians.
Thereby, has he committed an offence punishable under Section 279 IPC?

2 Point No.2:

sentences.text: Whether the prosecution proves beyond a reasonable doubt that on the aforementioned date, time, and place, the accused was a driver of Lorry No. AP 27 TU 3949 drove his lorry on FCI godown road near Sudheer way Bridge from Old Madras road towards FCI godown in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into pedestrian Sri. Venkateshappa.
Due to a collision, the pedestrian Venkatesappa sustained grievous blood injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Thereby, has the accused committed an offence punishable under Section 304(A) IPC?
Point No.3: What order?

10. My findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2: In the Negative Point No.3: As per the foregoing for the following reasons REASONS 11.
Points No.1 & 2
: As these two points are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts and discussion, they are taken together for common discussion.
In the instant case, the burden to prove the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt lies on the prosecution.
The prosecution shall establish that the accused drove his vehicle in a rash or negligent manner on a public road to endanger human safety and dashed into a pedestrian.
13. Learned Senior APP argued that the prosecution has proved its case against the accused beyond a reasonable doubt.
The prosecution witnesses supported the case of prosecution.
Hence, prayed for the conviction of the accused.
14. On the other hand, learned counsel for the accused argued that there is no corroboration available on record.
Prosecution witnesses fully supported the case.
Hence, prayed to acquit the accused.
15. Let me consider the oral and documentary evidence put forth by the prosecution.
To bring home the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt, the prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to PW.6 and marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

The prosecution has examined CW.3, Sri.
Charanraj, as PW1.
In his chief evidence, he deposed that the deceased Venkateshappa was his uncle.
He didn't remember the date.
His uncle succumbed to the accident.
He received a phone call from the police.
They showed his uncle's photographs.
Thereafter, he went to the boring hospital.
When the accident occurred, he was not in a spot.
He has not seen the accident in person, and he has also not identified the accused.
He has not given any statement to the police.
Treating this witness as a hostile, the learned Senior APP fully cross-examined him.
However, he denied all suggestions put to him.

sentences.text: The prosecution has examined CW.4, Sri. Vijay Kumar as PW.2.
In his chief evidence, he has also stated that he was not present on the spot when the accident occurred.
He has not seen that the accused by name Shankar Naik was the driver of the vehicle.
He has not given any statement to the police.
Treating this witness as a hostile, learned Senior APP fully cross- examined him.
However, he failed to prove anything contrary as he denied all suggestions put to him.
17. Thereafter, the prosecution has examined CW.1, Sri. Manjunath Naik, as PW.3.

In his chief evidence, he deposed on 07.01.2017 at 09.30 p.m, that he was working near Maramma Temple,
Hoskote Bus Stop.
At that time, an unknown person came to him and told him that near the Sudheer Bridge, there was an accident.

When he went to the spot and inquired, he came to know that Lorry No. AP27, TU 3949, Old Madras Road, near Sudeer Way Bridge, drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the pedestrians.
During his chief evidence, the complaint was marked as Ex.P.3 and his signature as Ex.P.3(a).
He identified the accused.

Treating this witness as partly hostile, learned Senior APP partly cross- examined him, wherein it was suggested that he had seen the accused drive his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner on an old Madras road towards FCI road and dashed to the pedestrian, and he had seen the occurrence in person.
He denied the suggestion.
During cross-examination by the defence also deposed that he had not seen the accident, and he went to the spot 5 minutes after the accident.
The prosecution has examined CW.4, Sri. Chalapathi, as PW.4.
he deposed that the police have not summoned him to the incident spot.
7 years ago, he signed the Ex.P.4.
The police obtained his signature, stating they had conducted post mortem.
He didn't know the contents of Ex.P.4.
Treating this witness as a partly hostile, learned Sr. APP, fully cross-examined him.
However, he denied all suggestions put to him.
Similarly, the prosecution examined CW.5, Sri. Devaraj, as PW.5.
In his chief evidence, he deposed that an unknown person called him and informed him about the accident.
He has not seen the accident, and he has also not identified the accused.
He has not given any statement to the police.
Treating this witness as hostile, learned Senior APP fully cross-examined him.
However, he denied all suggestions made to him.
19. The prosecution has examined CW.12, Sri. Mahesh Kanakagiri, as PW.6.
He is the Investigating Officer of this case.
During his chief evidence, he deposed on the procedure he followed during the investigation of this case.
During his cross- examination, he denied all suggestions put to him.
20. On perusal of the oral testimony of the prosecution witnesses, it could be seen that they have not identified the accused.
The presence of the accused and the rash of negligent driving by him remained unestablished by the prosecution through the evidence of these witnesses.
They have all turned hostile to the prosecution's case.
There is no corroboration available on record.
They have all made contrary statements.

sentences.text: As far as the documentary evidences are concerned, Ex. P.3 is the complaint.
It was marked through CW.1 that is PW.3.
It is pertinent to note that in a complaint, the CW.1 complainant has mentioned that on 07.01.2017 at 09.35 pm, there was an accident near the Sudheer Way Bridge.
There is no mention that he has seen the accident in person.
Similarly, during his chief evidence, he also deposed that he came to know about the accident through one person.
Though the prosecution has treated him as partly hostile and suggested that he had seen the accident.
However, he denied the suggestion.
For setting criminal law into motion by filing a complaint, his evidence may be considered.
22. Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar.
The mahazar witnesses turned hostile to the prosecution's case and did not support it.
Ex . P.7
is the hand sketch map.
According to this map, the lorry was taking a turn from Muthumari Amma temple towards the FCI.
At that time, the pedestrian was crossing the road towards Muthu Mariyamma Temple.
It is pertinent to note that whether there is any signal on the spot or a pedestrian way to cross the road is not forthcoming.
Ex.P.9 reflects that at the time of the accident, the accused was the driver of the vehicle, and he possessed a driving licence and his vehicle was duly insured.
Ex.P.10 is the inquest, and Ex.P.11 is the post-mortem report.
As per Ex.P.12 IMV report, no damages were recovered on the vehicle.
It was alleged that after the occurrence, the wheel of the lorry ran over the pedestrian.
However, there is no mention that in Ex.P.12 any blood stains on the wheel.
The accused did not dispute the death of the pedestrian.

However, he disputed C.C.
No. 13438/2017 his involvement and his rash or negligent driving.
The accused may be the driver of the vehicle as per Ex.P.9.

However, it is pertinent to note that none of the prosecution witnesses identified the accused as having driven the vehicle on the fateful day and in a rash or negligent manner, dashed into the pedestrian.
The ingredients of the alleged offence remained unestablished by the prosecution beyond a reasonable doubt.
23. At this juncture, it is pertinent to refer to Sections 279 and 304(A) IPC.
Section 279 of IPC-Rash driving or riding on a public way.

Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
304 (A) Causing death by negligence.

Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
24.
In the criminal case, the proof required is beyond a reasonable doubt, and the preponderance of probabilities is not sufficient.
It is well settled that, when two views are possible, one which favours the accused should be considered.
In other words, the benefit of doubt should go in favour of the accused.
The prosecution utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt.

ORDER
The accused is not found guilty of the alleged offences against him p/u/s.279 & 304(A) IPC.
